selected_versions: All four gateway sources are the admitted PMC version 1. No external lookup or version substitution occurred. Text/XML/metadata and supplement extractions are alternate artifacts of the same studies, not independent evidence.

sources.citation: Pani et al. Diabetes Care 2008;31:1991-1996. DOI 10.2337/dc08-0577.
sources.population: FOS n=2473, predominantly white adults >=25, excluding antidiabetic treatment or FPG>=126; NHANES 2001-2004 n=3270, adults >=25, no self-reported diabetes, FPG<126 and available HbA1c. NHANES is closer to the task's diagnosis/glucose selection, but neither cohort is this Mexico design.
sources.measurement: DCCT-standardized HPLC HbA1c in percent; hexokinase plasma glucose mg/dL. Not serum glucose as requested. The authors report assay/population differences between FOS and NHANES.

statistics.locator: Results, paragraph beginning 'There was no difference in BMI'; multivariable regression summary
statistics.adjustment: NHANES: sex, BMI and fasting glucose. FOS additionally 2-h postload glucose.
statistics.uncertainty: No slope SE or CI in admitted main-text summary. Do not use a p-value as a precision weight.
statistics.use: Use the NHANES 0.010/year as the HbA1c conditional location age coefficient, subject to A5 and output truncation. FOS is contextual corroboration, not pooled as a replicate of NHANES.

statistics.locator: Results first paragraph and paragraph on age-category BMI differences
statistics.adjustment: Descriptive sample summaries; NHANES survey weighting applies to its analyses.
statistics.uncertainty: Main text labels small plus/minus values as SD, but this is not used as individual BMI spread; no reliable individual BMI SD is taken from this item.
statistics.use: 28.01 is the pre-truncation BMI mean and centering value by transfer assumption A2. The statement of no BMI differences across age categories motivates a simplified age-independent law; it does not establish independence or sex equivalence.

statistics.adjustment: Age-specific descriptive weighted means and quantiles, not covariate-conditioned intercepts.
statistics.uncertainty: Mean uncertainties are SEs; quantile CI is not supplied in this table. FOS distributions differ. Main-text/abstract youngest-tail descriptions differ; Table 1 is the chosen locator.
statistics.use: Mean 5.40 supplies level context for the assumed reference location, not an equality fit. Tail values inform a moderate residual scale; no SE-to-SD conversion or quantile fit is attempted.

statistics.locator: Results, IFG frequency and age-related fasting glucose paragraphs
statistics.use: Context only, not a fitted target for this equal-cell design. Underlying source joint ages, glucose and BMI are unavailable.

sources.declined: No longitudinal 0.024-0.043/year effects are used as cross-sectional coefficients. Do not infer source BMI or HbA1c SD from reported SEs. The unadmitted online appendix is not retrieved.

sources.citation: Huang et al. Int J Environ Res Public Health 2021;18:3390. DOI 10.3390/ijerph18073390.
sources.population: Taiwan Biobank adults 30-70 without prior diabetes diagnosis, n=4748; fasting not universal; no FPG<126 eligibility rule. Methods report 2563 women but results/tables report 2565 (2183 men); this inconsistency is retained and no count is used for synthesis.
sources.measurement: HbA1c percentage from K2EDTA venous blood; relevant results do not adjust for glucose or BMI.

statistics.locator: Table 1, multiple regression on age and sex
statistics.use: Qualitative context for a small sex difference; no direct coefficient transfer to glucose/BMI-adjusted HbA1c. The assumed female effect -0.04 is not reported by this paper.

statistics.locator: Table 4, HbA1c<6.5 subgroup; Table 6, age bins
statistics.uncertainty: These are individual marginal SDs, not conditional residual SDs; subgroup SDs are affected by HbA1c selection.
statistics.use: Magnitude context only for residual SD assumption 0.32 and allowance of discordance. Do not import the HbA1c<6.5 restriction or the 12.7 maximum into the target.

sources.declined: Age/sex-specific slopes and apparent male plateau are unadjusted and do not identify the target conditional interaction. No interaction is imposed, but this omission is explicit A5. The overall 0.61 SD and high-HbA1c mixture are not fitted because fasting and diabetes selection differ.

sources.population: Adults 30-64 in selected Finnish cities: Health 2011 general population n=653; Maamu Russian n=293, Somali n=184, Kurdish n=275. Excludes diabetes by registers, diagnoses, medication, HbA1c>=6.5 or fasting glucose>=7 mmol/L; complete variables and fasting 4-17 h. Stricter diabetes/HbA1c restrictions and wider fasting window than task.
sources.measurement: Standing measured BMI; immunoturbidimetric HbA1c; glucose serum in the general Finnish group and fluoride-citrate plasma in Maamu groups. General-population serum slopes selected for closer measurement alignment. Supplement S2 outcome scale is HbA1c percent as supported by intercept about 5.1 and main Table 1's dual-unit reporting.

statistics.locator: Additional file 3 Table S1, Age+sex+BMI, General population column; page 1 of admitted page extraction
statistics.adjustment: Age binary 30-44 vs 45-64, sex, continuous BMI; main methods state glucose analyses additionally adjusted for fasting time (not displayed as a coefficient in S1). Inverse probability weights and stratified sampling.
statistics.uncertainty: No coefficient SE/CI in S1. Band midpoints are approximations, not observed within-band means.
statistics.use: BMI 0.432 mg/dL per kg/m^2 and sex 4.4496 mg/dL after rounded factor 18. Continuous age coefficient 0.1985*18/17.5=0.204171428571 mg/dL/year is derived under A4. Source intercept is declined because age coding, fasting and population differ.

statistics.locator: Additional file 3 Table S2, Age+sex+BMI, General population column; page 2 of admitted page extraction
statistics.adjustment: Binary age and sex, without glucose. Survey-weighted linear regression.
statistics.uncertainty: No BMI SE or CI; no source glucose-adjusted BMI-HbA1c result is supplied.
statistics.use: 0.0125 pp per BMI unit informs the untruncated total BMI association in A6, equivalent to 0.0625 pp/5 units. It is not inserted as the glucose-adjusted coefficient. Sex contrast conflicts with the Taiwanese marginal pattern, underscoring transport/adjustment uncertainty.

statistics.locator: Supplement S2 Age+sex+BMI across origin columns; main Methods, Results, Table 3 and limitations
statistics.use: Heterogeneity and selection context, not independent pooled replications or a reason to set nonsignificant effects to zero. R2 values are not converted into residual SDs without covariate distributions.

sources.declined: No categorical BMI, waist, WHR or WHtR law is imported. Supplement has some label/sign anomalies outside selected BMI rows; those cells are not repaired or used. The internally described approximately 8% plasma-serum difference is not imposed as a universal measurement conversion. S1 and S2 share participants and do not provide independent precision.

sources.citation: A Comparison of HbA1c and Fasting Blood Sugar Tests in General Population. Int J Prev Med 2010;1:187-194.
sources.population: Kerman, Iran cluster sample, ages 18-75, n=604; FBS<=126 subgroup n=525 includes 30 people with self-reported diabetes. Target excludes reported prior diagnosis and requires strict FPG<126 and 8-12 h fasting. No exclusion equivalence is assumed.
sources.measurement: Single fasting blood sugar by enzyme method and HbA1c by Biosystem kit. Fasting-hour distribution and assay equivalence to the target are unavailable.

statistics.locator: Results paragraph on subgroup Pearson correlation; Table 1 nondiabetic column
statistics.adjustment: Crude subgroup Pearson correlation and descriptive moments, no covariate adjustment.
statistics.uncertainty: Rounded r and SDs; source reports p<0.001 for correlation but not its CI. Derived slope has no assigned precision.
statistics.use: Slope magnitude is used under explicit crude-to-conditional and cross-population assumption A6. Neither r=0.23 nor SD_HbA1c=0.73 is claimed reproduced by the target model, whose source-selected HbA1c spread differs.

statistics.locator: Table 2, FBS<=126, prediction of HbA1c based on FBS
statistics.adjustment: Adjusted model names age, sex and BMI.
statistics.use: Declined as a numerical parameter: 0.13 differs by factor 9.600952948183 from the dimensionally derived crude slope using Table 1 SDs and Results r. No supplied scale explanation resolves the discrepancy. Do not reinterpret 0.09 as pp/mg/dL, standardized beta, per-10-unit effect or a typo.

sources.declined: Do not import screening cutoffs, diagnostic accuracy or diabetic-subgroup relationships. Narrative/table sex percentages differ, so sex counts are not used.

overlap: Source E1 contains two distinct cohorts, whose assay/selection differences are preserved. PMC8038122 cites Pani but its own Taiwan observations are separate. All artifacts of PMC6458679 describe the same four study groups; S1/S2 and main tables share samples. No evidence precision is pooled and no repeated citation is counted as a new cohort.

assumptions.canonical_definitions: model_spec.json assumptions A1-A9 are part of this submission and state the full assumptions.
assumptions.A1: Fixed equal cells and uniform within-band ages.
assumptions.A2: BMI mean transfer, CV/support, age/sex independence.
assumptions.A5: HbA1c age transfer, intercept/sex assumption and no interaction.
assumptions.A6: Crude-to-conditional glucose slope and BMI decomposition.
assumptions.A7: Conditional independence and unmeasured residual factors.
assumptions.A8: Tail families, support and HbA1c residual SD.
assumptions.A9: Selected-population membership without unmeasured screening-field validation.
